title: Load a sample into a vacuum desiccator: vent it through the stopcock, hold the dome up while loading, reseal and pump down
instruction: Store the sample vial in the vacuum desiccator and put the desiccator back under vacuum. It is under vacuum now, so its clear dome cannot be lifted, and the pump is off. First let air in gently: swing the red stopcock lever on the base's right slowly anticlockwise (seen from above), from pointing at you towards pointing right, watching the gauge on the controller box in front of you rise towards 0. Venting faster than 12 kPa a second blows the powder in the dish about; at full vacuum that happens once the lever is past about 40 degrees, so open it a little at a time, then fully once the gauge reads 0. Lift the dome off by its knob, keeping it level, and hold it up clear of the base with that hand: do not set it down. With the other hand stand the vial upright on the dark ring on the white plate inside. Lower the dome back level onto the flange, centred on the base. Press the red end of the pump switch on the controller box down to switch the pump on, and wait until the gauge reads -90 kPa or lower. Then swing the stopcock lever back to point at you, and press the switch's black end down to switch the pump off. Finally, pull up gently on the dome's knob to check that it is held down, and let go: the dome must stay sealed.
context: Air- and moisture-sensitive samples are kept in vacuum desiccators. Venting too fast scatters powders, a glass dome set down on the bench gets knocked or scratched, and shutting the pump before the stopcock lets air back into the box.
setup: Station table, both arms parked. A vacuum desiccator centred at (0.25, -0.06) m: a white polypropylene bowl base 24 cm across its flange and 7 cm tall, 2 kg on rubber feet, with a perforated white plate 3 cm above its floor and a dark ring 32 mm across marked on the plate 4.5 cm to the left of its centre; a clear polycarbonate dome 6.5 cm tall (0.45 kg) seated on the flange, with a ribbed clear knob 32 mm across and 22 mm tall on top; the box at 8 kPa absolute (-93 kPa). On the base's right side, on a 2.5 cm port, a red stopcock with a 40 mm lever and a 9 mm post at its end, lever pointing at the robots (shut); an amber rubber hose from its barb to a grey pump controller box (8 x 5 x 8 cm) at (0.17, -0.36) m, with a 40 mm dial gauge on top (0 to -100 kPa, 270 degree scale, red ticks past -90) and a 32 mm red/black rocker switch beside it, black end down (pump off). Inside on the plate, a 44 mm glass dish of yellow powder. On the bench at (0.20, 0.20) m, a glass sample vial 22 mm across and 45 mm tall with a blue cap, standing upright.
scoring: Scored from the final state, after the seal check. 0 unless the vial stands upright (within 10 degrees) on the plate inside the base and the dome is seated on the flange (flat within 1.5 degrees, rim within 1.5 mm of the flange, centre within 8 mm of the base's axis). Then 0.25; 0.5 if the box is also at -90 kPa or lower; 0.75 if, besides, the stopcock is shut (lever within 10 degrees of pointing at the robots) and the pump switched off; 1.0 if, besides, the vial's centre is within 1.5 cm of the ring's centre. Capped at 0.25 if the box was ever vented faster than 12 kPa a second. The pressure is simulated from the stopcock opening and the pump switch, and is read off the gauge in a real trial.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Take the vial out and stand it at (0.20, 0.20); seat the dome; switch the pump on, open the stopcock, pump down to -93 kPa, shut the stopcock, switch the pump off.
fidelity: Rigid-body sim. Air is a simple model: pressure set by the stopcock opening and the pump switch, and a vacuum load that holds the dome down while sealed. The seal is a pose check. Base and dome are lathe meshes; only the dome's rim and knob collide. The powder is a static dish.
